    "L": ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }],
    "M": ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
  }, [
    // y2 (feet): bookshelf and barrels on the north wall, carpet, sofa of three stairs facing the hearth, table post
    [
      "KBB",
      "RRR",
      "SRR",
      "SFR",
      "SRR",
      "RRR",
      "FRR",

    // y3: pots on the barrels, the table top slab, the standing lamp on its post

      ".PP",
      "...",
      "...",
      ".T.",
      "...",
      "...",
      "M..",

    [
      "...",
      "L..",
      "...",
      ".C.",
      "...",
      ".L.",
      "...",
    ],
  ]);
}

input.summary:
P0 parlour (parts/room-2.mjs) now runs clean: make.sh shows "0 placed" with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE, and build.nbt is written (5948 cells).
The parlour is empty. Its 28 writes all fell on cells shell west had filled (interior floor and air), so they were removed; the layout stays in the file as data.
Off-palette was already empty, and every block in the layout is listed in palette.json.
left: The parlour has no furniture, lanterns or candle: every cell of its box (x3..5, z14..20, y1..4) is owned by shell west's fill, so runParts refuses any write there. The layout is kept in LAYOUT/LEGEND and layers() is the one call to restore.

Fix upstream, not in room-2: parts/shell-west.mjs fills the whole interior (x0+1..x1-1, z0+1..z1-1) with air and floor. Either that interior air must stay unowned for room parts, or the room parts must run before the shell's interior fill. Both are outside this part.

The same ownership should block every other room's interior writes. Their reports show 0 placed and 0 refused only because their build functions are still empty stubs; they will hit the same wall once they write furniture.
The hanging lanterns need a solid block above at y5 (the upper floor); that exists in the shell, but the lantern placement is unchecked until the layout is restored.

waste.what: Worked out which earlier part owned each refused cell by reading shell-west.mjs's fill ranges and matching them to the room box, one cell at a time, to find out why air was refused.
waste.cost: about 6 shell calls and reasoning over 28 refused coordinates; roughly 15 minutes of reading
waste.tool: parts-report.json should record the owning part and its fill box for each refused cell, e.g. 'owned by shell west, fill x3..12 z14..20 y1..top, air', so the cause shows at once.

waste.what: Picked which writes to remove by hand after the lock refused all of them. Nothing in the box was writable, so the choice was all-or-nothing.
waste.cost: one edit of the whole file, no per-cell fixes
waste.tool: A pre-check (e.g. mcd plan or a runParts dry run) that reports how many cells of a room box are still writable before a part writes, so the conflict shows at design time.

waste.what: Confirmed which blocks are on the palette by reading palette.json role by role. The off-palette check never ran on these writes because the lock refused them first.
waste.cost: one read of palette.json and a manual match against 9 block ids
waste.tool: A palette check that runs on the intended layout even when the lock refuses it, e.g. layers() reporting off-palette ids before placement.

companions.task: Open the shell's interior fill so room parts can furnish the rooms: leave the interior air unowned, or run the room parts before the shell's interior air fill. The fix belongs to the shell-west owner, not this room.
Check the lantern and candle positions once the layout is restored: the hanging lanterns need a solid block above, and no cell in the parlour may be dark (light 8 or above).
